confusions: SpecialMove.move is proto3 `optional` — could mean either 'explicit presence tracking for a field that's always logically present' or 'genuinely absent for some Role values (e.g. a THREAT that references a square rather than a concrete move)'; I assumed the latter.

PinGeometry.pinned_to could naturally be read two ways: (a) the piece/king shielded behind the pinned piece along the pin line (the classic pin target), or (b) the square/piece the pinned piece would be forced to move to; I picked (a) as the standard chess-pin meaning.

SpecialMove.Role.ROLE_REPLY vs ROLE_CONTINUATION compete for 'the next move in a sequence' — REPLY suggesting the opponent's response and CONTINUATION suggesting the same side extending its own plan; I split them along whose move it is.

TargetFan vs ConvergingFan read as deliberate opposites (one-to-many vs many-to-one), so 'source'/'target' naming in TargetFan could theoretically be swapped (targets fanning out to a source) but the PieceSet-as-plural-field convention made the one-to-many reading much more natural.

ConvergingFan's target oneof (target_piece vs target_square) raises whether 'square' is used only when the square is empty (e.g. a mating square or escape square) versus always being an alternate encoding of the same occupied square as target_piece; I assumed the empty-square case.

guesses.expected_docstring: A profile variant identifying the move actually played on the board (as opposed to a threatened, alternative, or hypothetical move), used when the board event's semantics are fully captured by 'this move happened.'
The move that was played, in the engine's standard move representation (from-square, to-square, promotion, etc.).
A profile variant describing a single move that carries a distinguished semantic role in the analysis (mate, threat, refutation, etc.), independent of whether that move was the one actually played.
The move being highlighted; explicit-presence optional because for some roles the move may not be resolved to a concrete move (e.g. only a role/threat is known without a specific line).
Which special role this move plays in the position (mating move, threat, reply, etc.).
Default zero-value indicating no role was set; should not appear in valid output.
The move delivers checkmate.
The move represents a threat that would be carried out if the opponent does not respond to it.
The move is the opponent's response to a preceding move being explained.
The move is a further move by the same side continuing an established plan or line, following on from a prior move.
The move is an alternative candidate to the main line being shown, offered for comparison.
The move refutes (disproves the soundness of) a preceding move, threat, or plan.
The move is a pawn push that is part of an aggressive pawn-storm advance against the opposing king.
A profile variant describing one piece (the source) that relates to — e.g. attacks or covers — a fan-out set of multiple target pieces.
The single piece from which the fan-out relationship originates (e.g. the attacking or covering piece).
The set of pieces that the source piece targets (e.g. is simultaneously attacking or covering).
A profile variant describing multiple pieces (the sources) that converge on a single target piece or square, either as attackers or defenders — the mirror image of TargetFan.
The single piece that all the source pieces converge on, when the target square is occupied by a specific piece.
The square that all the source pieces converge on, used when the target is an empty square (e.g. a mating or escape square) rather than an occupied piece.
The set of pieces converging on the target (the multiple attackers or defenders).
Whether the converging source pieces are attacking or defending the target.
Default zero-value indicating no role was set; should not appear in valid output.
The converging pieces are all attacking the target.
The converging pieces are all defending the target.
A profile variant holding a collection of square ranges (line segments on the board), used to highlight multiple rays, files, ranks, or diagonals at once.
The list of individual square ranges making up this collection.
A profile variant describing the three-piece geometry of a pin: the pinned piece, the piece executing the pin, and the piece shielded behind the pin.
The piece that is pinned and therefore restricted from moving freely.
The piece executing the pin along the line (typically a bishop, rook, or queen).
The piece behind the pinned piece on the same line that would be exposed to capture or check if the pinned piece moved (often the king).
